content.title: Inference now drives two-thirds of AI workloads, changing where chips get deployed
content.summary: Inference now accounts for about two-thirds of AI workloads, overtaking training which previously dominated at 85% in 2023. This shift is driving infrastructure decisions toward modular data centers and commodity‑memory chip designs, exemplified by Positron AI Inc.'s Atlas and Titan servers and Oracle Corp.'s deployment of 340 Atlas units in its cloud.

content.title: Sovereign AI: Where control becomes an architectural requirement
content.summary: The article discusses the growing need for sovereign AI, emphasizing that organizations must control the systems that generate intelligence and the data they handle. It highlights gaps in vendor claims, the cost of adding isolated environments, and notes that AWS scores low on customer‑run air‑gapped stacks, while theCUBE Research is mentioned as a research platform.

content.title: Sovereignty starts with data, not chips, says Stuttgart AI factory chief
content.summary: Stuttgart’s HammerHAI AI factory, built on a Hewlett Packard Enterprise system with Nvidia GPUs, prioritizes SMEs and startups by offering sovereign, lock‑in‑free access and a concierge model that pairs each customer with a consistent contact. The facility emphasizes human‑centric design, allowing workloads to move freely to or from hyperscalers, and is highlighted alongside theCUBE AI Video Cloud and theCUBEai.com neural network in the article.

content.title: A tale of two Nvidias
content.summary: Nvidia reported strong earnings but said it has no plans for former CEO Jensen Huang to return, while investors and tech leaders like Elon Musk are pushing for his comeback. Meanwhile, Nvidia announced it will no longer sell its H200 chips in China, citing export restrictions and remote access concerns.

content.title: Signal restricts mobile screenshots as it confronts ‘existential threat’ of AI surveillance
content.summary: Signal has restricted screenshot functionality on its Android and iOS apps to counter the risk of AI agents scanning user screens, a move prompted by concerns over privacy breaches from operating systems like Windows, Android, and macOS/iOS. The company allows users to disable the restriction, though this would compromise its privacy guarantees, and acknowledges the solution is incomplete.

source.name: The Decoder
content.title: AI coding agents ace isolated tests but complete fewer than one in ten tasks in a simulated workplace
content.summary: AI coding agents such as Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra achieve high scores on standard benchmarks but complete fewer than one in ten tasks in a simulated workplace environment. Anthropic reports that its Claude model writes over 80% of the company's production code, indicating growing success for AI coding agents.

source.name: The Decoder
content.title: AI is getting better faster than experts can reliably test whether new systems are safe, METR warns
content.summary: The AI research organization METR warns that AI models are improving faster than experts can test their safety, potentially leaving humans unable to assess catastrophic risks. METR found that while models already outperform professionals on well-defined coding tasks, they still struggle with open-ended questions and may overestimate performance in real-world use.

content.title: Perplexity's new Monitor API turns web search from a one-off query into a nonstop watchdog
content.summary: Perplexity has launched a Monitor API that schedules web searches and sends relevant updates to AI agents via webhook, outperforming competitors like Firecrawl and Exa in internal tests. The service, priced at $1 per 1,000 requests, tracks topics or pages, filters results with a decision model, and is positioned for use cases such as tracking funding rounds and staffing changes.

content.title: Security researchers show how cheap AI inference providers steal keys and snoop on users
content.summary: Dragos researchers sent roughly 2 million AI requests containing fake credentials to AI providers, uncovering major security flaws that let attackers steal credentials undetected for months. The study highlighted intermediaries such as OpenRouter and model marketplaces like Novita, AtlasCloud, and StreamLake as weak links, and showed that even major US providers failed to enforce privacy settings, with attackers using tools like ARTEX to harvest AWS keys and test them quickly.

content.title: The UN fails to agree on rules regulating ‘killer robots’
content.summary: UN diplomats in Geneva failed to agree on binding rules for autonomous weapons, agreeing instead to start discussing options within two years. The negotiations were stalled by Russia, Israel, and the US, while humanitarian groups and the International Committee of the Red Cross urged urgent legally binding regulations.

content.title: Banks Have Had It Up to Here With Your AI Agent
content.summary: Wells Fargo will enforce new terms warning customers that using AI agents is at their own risk, joining Citibank and PNC in tightening policies. The move follows incidents where agents posted sensitive data, and other firms such as Amazon, Meta’s Muse, United, and American Express have also restricted or responded to AI‑powered purchasing.
